steps.say: Testicular torsion is caused by abnormal testicular fixation. A bell-clapper deformity is present silently from birth. The cord is free to twist inside the vaginal sac. Intravaginal rotation is completed with movement or cold. Venous outflow is blocked before arterial inflow. Pain and swelling are produced within minutes.
steps.tx: **Testicular torsion** (cord twisting cutoff) follows a high investing **bell-clapper deformity** (free hanging bell), where the tunica vaginalis grips high and lets the cord twist inside the sac, an **intravaginal rotation** (inside sac spin). The twist first blocks venous outflow, so swelling and pain explode within minutes.

vis.alt: Diagram comparing testicular torsion, acute epididymo-orchitis, and appendix torsion.
vis.caption: Bell-clapper torsion cuts venous outflow first: minutes count. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The golden window for testicular salvage is 6 hours. Rescue above 90 percent is achieved within the window. Salvage below 10 percent is expected after 24 hours. Overnight waiting is never advised for scrotal pain. Each hour of twist is known to kill tubules. Immediate exploration is arranged without delay.
steps.tx: The **golden window** (salvage countdown) for **testicular salvage** (testis rescue) is **6 hours** (six) from pain onset with rescue above **90%** (nine in ten), crashing under **10%** (one in ten) after **24 hours** (a full day). Never watch and wait for morning, because each hour of twist kills more tubules.

steps.say: Manual detorsion is attempted promptly while theatre is prepared. Open-book rotation is applied from the foot of the bed. The right testis is turned gently counter-clockwise. The left testis is turned gently clockwise. Bilateral orchidopexy is performed regardless of tissue viability. Residual twist is excluded carefully at operation.
steps.tx: **Manual detorsion** (twist back by hand) turns **open-book** (pages outward) fashion, right testis counter-clockwise and left clockwise seen from the feet, then fixes both sides with **bilateral orchidopexy** (both testes stitched) regardless of viability. Relieve pain first does not replace theatre, because residual twist persists.

steps.say: Torsion of the appendix testis is recognised by the blue dot. The hydatid of Morgagni is twisted on its stalk. A blue spot is seen through the upper scrotal skin. Rest and analgesia are prescribed for classic cases. Exploration is reserved for doubtful presentations. The testis itself is unaffected by the episode.
steps.tx: Twisted **appendix testis** (stalked nubbin, **hydatid of Morgagni** (Morgagni remnant)) shows the **blue dot sign** (blue spot) through the upper scrotal skin and settles with rest unless the diagnosis wavers. Spare the knife when the dot is classic, because exploration adds nothing.

steps.say: Acute epididymo-orchitis is distinguished carefully from torsion clinically. Pain relief on elevation is known as Prehn sign. Hypervascularity is demonstrated on colour Doppler. Low resistive index is recorded carefully in the inflamed vessels. Antibiotics are prescribed once flow is confirmed. Exploration is avoided entirely when infection is clear.
steps.tx: Acute **epididymo-orchitis** (tube and testis infection) eases with elevation, a positive **Prehn sign** (lift relief), and shows **hypervascularity** (extra blood flow) with low resistance on colour Doppler. Treat the infection, not the twist, once flow proves present, because unnecessary exploration scars.

steps.say: Epididymitis causes are divided by the age of 35 years. Chlamydia trachomatis is found commonly in younger men. Gonococcal infection is tested by urethral swab. Escherichia coli is isolated in older men. Coliform gut organisms are cultured from midstream urine. Treatment is matched carefully to the organism found.
steps.tx: Under **35 years** (thirty five), epididymitis is usually sexually transmitted **Chlamydia trachomatis** (chlamydia) and gonococcus, while over 35 it is coliform gut organisms, chiefly **Escherichia coli** (E. coli). Swab young men and culture older men, because treatment differs entirely. Add a urethral swab and first void urine test in the young group.

steps.say: Hydrocele is diagnosed by a transilluminating scrotal swelling. Serous fluid is trapped between the vaginal layers. Tumour is excluded first by careful examination. Jaboulay eversion is performed through a scrotal incision. Lord plication is selected for smaller thin sacs. Blind stitching is avoided entirely when malignancy is suspected.
steps.tx: **Hydrocele** (water around the testis) pools serous fluid between the tunica vaginalis layers and is cured by **Jaboulay eversion** (sac inside out) or **Lord plication** (sac gathered) stitching. Confirm transillumination first and rule out tumour by examination, because a malignant hydrocele must not be stitched blindly.

vis.alt: Illustration of the transillumination test glowing through a hydrocele, with transilluminant and non-transilluminant causes compared.
vis.caption: A hydrocele glows brilliantly on transillumination: confirm this before Jaboulay eversion or Lord plication. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Spermatocele is recognised clinically as a benign epididymal cyst. Dead sperm are contained in efferent ductule cysts. Separation from the testis is felt on examination. Spermatocelectomy is offered only for pain or doubt. Reassurance is given confidently for the majority. Change over time is monitored by regular review.
steps.tx: **Spermatocele** (sperm cyst) is a benign retention cyst of the **efferent ductules** (sperm exit tubes) or epididymis holding dead sperm, separate from the testis, removed by **spermatocelectomy** (cyst excision) only when painful or doubtful. Reassure the rest, because most never change.
